pesto.title: Kitchen to Table — Basil Pesto in 5 Weeks
pesto.excerpt: A simple recipe series showing how to go from pod to plate with your first PlantyHub harvest.
body: Your first basil pods usually tip into harvest mode around week three to five — snip the top leaves and the plant keeps pushing new growth.
For a weeknight pesto, blend a generous handful of fresh basil with olive oil, garlic, pine nuts and hard cheese until silky. Taste for salt and lemon.
The difference from supermarket herbs is immediate: brighter aroma, softer bitterness, and pesto that tastes like the garden instead of the fridge.

hydroponics.title: Why Hydroponics Uses 90% Less Water
hydroponics.excerpt: The science behind smart indoor gardens and why they're the sustainable choice for urban homes.
body: In soil gardens, water escapes through runoff and evaporation. A closed hydroponic tray recirculates what the roots actually need.
HomeGarder One dosed lighting and steady moisture mean plants spend energy on leaves, not on surviving dry spells.
For apartment growers, that translates to fewer top-ups, less waste, and herbs that stay productive for months.

spices.title: Aromatic Spices You Can Grow on the Counter
spices.excerpt: Thyme, oregano, rosemary, chives and chili — the spice drawer, reinvented as living pods.
body: Culinary spices do not have to arrive dried. Slow-growing aromatics like thyme, oregano and rosemary thrive under steady LED light.
Chives give you a cut-and-come-again onion note for eggs and soups. Chili pods bring heat once fruits begin to colour.
Fill a few holes with our spice pods — or grab the 12-pod spice mix — and season straight from the canopy while dinner is on the hob.

first-harvest.title: How to Take Your First Harvest Without Stress
first-harvest.excerpt: A calm checklist for week two and three: what to snip, what to leave, and how often to feed.
body: Wait until plants have several true leaves before the first cut. Never remove more than a third of the canopy at once.
Harvest in the morning when oils are concentrated. Use clean scissors and cut just above a leaf node to encourage branching.
Keep the nutrient solution topped up and the light cycle consistent — a stressed plant tastes bitter long before it looks unhealthy.

partnership.title: PlantyHub × Sustainable Living EU
partnership.excerpt: We teamed up with eco-conscious creators to show how one garden can change your daily routine.
body: Together with Sustainable Living EU we followed households swapping weekly herb packets for a countertop garden.
Creators logged setup time, water top-ups and flavour notes — most were cooking with their own cut greens inside a month.
The takeaway was simple: when growing is automatic, fresh seasoning stops being a special occasion.

earthday.title: Earth Day: Grow Your Own, Waste Less
earthday.excerpt: How biodegradable pods and home growing help cut plastic and food waste.
body: Store-bought soft herbs often wilt unused. Growing only what you snip means flavour without the half-empty clamshell.
Our pods are designed to compost after the grow cycle, and the garden itself is built to last years of refills.
Small kitchen gardens will not solve climate change alone — but they change habits, and habits scale.

faqItems.q: Do I need any gardening experience?
faqItems.a: None at all. Drop in a pod, add water and nutrients, and the LED runs on an automatic 16/8 cycle. The pod guides walk you through every step.

faqItems.q: How long until my first harvest?
faqItems.a: Most herbs and spices are ready to pick in about 2–3 weeks, and keep producing for months afterwards.

faqItems.q: How much electricity does it use?
faqItems.a: Very little — the full-spectrum LED is as efficient as a couple of household bulbs, roughly a few euros a month.

faqItems.q: What can I grow in it?
faqItems.a: Basil, mint, parsley, cilantro, dill, arugula and more — 12 pods at once. Any HomeGarder pod fits the slots.

faqItems.q: Is it covered by a warranty?
faqItems.a: Yes — a 2-year warranty plus a 30-day money-back guarantee if it's not for you.
